name: SIGMA - Asymmetric Outbound Connection Volume (Possible Exfiltration) [threshold]
description: Elastic threshold companion for rules/sigma/net_zeek_conn_outbound_volume_asymmetry.yml (issue #441 Part B). Alerts when a single source (source.ip) produces >=3 flows matching the asymmetric shape (source.bytes>=5000000 AND destination.bytes<=200000, event.dataset:zeek.conn) within a 30-minute lookback (a 15-minute run interval with lookback >= interval + the 15-minute detection window, guaranteeing full containment for any campaign phase - same overlap-safety math as net-zeek-ssh-session-cadence.ndjson/auth-win-bruteforce-source-spray.ndjson, applied from the start rather than found-and-fixed later). One high-ratio flow is ordinary (video calls, backups, large uploads) - the REPETITION from one source is the signal this threshold rule adds; the Sigma file is the single-flow logic-of-record and is deliberately status:experimental so deploy_detections.sh does not also deploy it as a noisy per-flow query rule. KNOWN LIMITATION (documented on the Sigma file too): source.bytes/destination.bytes thresholds are an absolute-value APPROXIMATION of asymmetry, not a true ratio - Lucene cannot express orig_bytes/resp_bytes as a computed ratio, only independent field-level range queries. Thresholds (5MB up, 200KB down, 3 occurrences) are a starting point, not a validated baseline for any specific deployment - expect tuning against real traffic before relying on this in production. Not live-verified end to end (no live Elasticsearch in the environment this was written in).
author: Suburban-SOC
false_positives: A large one-way upload that is entirely legitimate - cloud backup/sync, video/photo upload, a large email attachment, a VoIP/video call's outbound leg, or a CI/CD artifact push, repeated a handful of times in one session (e.g. a sync client uploading several large files back to back).
A single ordinary asymmetric flow is expected occasionally - only sustained repetition from one source is meant to be actioned.
